design_contract.scope: A Bayesian model consists of a measurable parameter space $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$, prior probability $\Pi$, measurable observation space $(\mathsf Y,\mathcal Y)$, and probability kernel $K(\theta,\cdot)$ with $\theta\mapsto K(\theta,B)$ measurable for every $B\in\mathcal Y$. The generic MSF model is only an indexed family; use the new `MSF-01 def-parameter-measurable-statistical-model-as-markov-kernel` when that family is to be mixed. Form joint law $\Pi(d\theta)K(\theta,dy)$ by kernel integration. For a measurable observation random element $Y$, define posterior initially as an $\Omega$-indexed RCD of $\theta$ given $\sigma(Y)$; its existence requires standard-Borel $\Theta$ and the inspected RCD theorem (AC here means Axiom of Choice). This is not yet a kernel indexed by every $y\in\mathsf Y$. When $\mathsf Y$ is standard Borel, factor the RCD through $Y$ with the inspected factorization lemma/disintegration theorem to obtain a measurable posterior kernel $y\mapsto\Pi_y$; on null conditioning values its version is not uniquely determined. For a dominated model, BCS-02's jointly measurable likelihood-density formula separately yields a data-indexed kernel on valid evidence fibers with the stated filler elsewhere, without using that standard-Borel observation-space route. Distinguish RCD, data-indexed posterior kernel, density formula, and null-fiber versions.
design_contract.proof_route: Product-kernel construction and RCD existence; when claiming a $y$-indexed kernel from an RCD, use `lem-regular-conditional-kernels-factor-through-a-standard-borel-conditioning-variable` or `thm-disintegration-of-a-joint-law-on-standard-borel-spaces` with both spaces standard Borel; carry the supplier's Axiom-of-Choice premise.

design_contract.scope: For a prior measure $\Pi$ on $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ and nonnegative measurable likelihood section $L_y$, define $Z(y)=\int L_y(\theta)\Pi(d\theta)$. On a fixed observation fibre the normalized measure is a probability exactly when $0<Z(y)<\infty$. For a proper prior, the almost-everywhere result additionally requires that $(\theta,y)\mapsto L_y(\theta)$ be jointly measurable and be a normalized sampling-kernel density against a sigma-finite data measure $\nu$; separate RN versions indexed by $\theta$ do not by themselves imply joint measurability. Then Tonelli gives $\int Z(y)\nu(dy)=1$, so normalization holds on the prior-predictive full-measure set where $Z>0$; zero/infinite fibres receive only the existing RCD filler, not a pointwise learned posterior. For a sigma-finite improper prior, prove the finite-positive normalizer statement locally and distinguish it from a prior-predictive probability. Give flat-prior known-variance Normal mean posterior $N(\bar y,\sigma^2/n)$ for $n\ge1$; show improper Beta$(0,0)$ Binomial posterior diverges at an endpoint when $y=0$ or $y=n$.
design_contract.proof_route: Reuse the existing Bayes-kernel theorem for proper priors, Tonelli for almost-everywhere normalization, and explicit integration/completing the square for examples. Never form a quotient at zero/infinite evidence.
design_contract.examples: valid finite evidence, prior-predictive null fiber, improper flat prior yielding proper posterior, improper Beta endpoint divergence.

design_contract.scope: State the sufficient exponential-family update direction: for IID data with likelihood density $h(y)\exp\{\eta(\theta)^TT(y)-A(\theta)\}$ against a declared data measure and prior density proportional to $\exp\{\eta(\theta)^T\chi-\nu A(\theta)\}$ against a declared parameter measure, update $\chi$ by $\sum_iT(y_i)$ and $\nu$ by $n$, only when the prior and posterior normalizers are finite positive. Define the proper laws used in the examples: Beta$(\alpha,\beta)$ has density $p^{\alpha-1}(1-p)^{\beta-1}/B(\alpha,\beta)$ on $(0,1)$; Gamma$(a,b)$ is shape-rate with density $b^a\lambda^{a-1}e^{-b\lambda}/\Gamma(a)$ on $(0,\infty)$; Poisson$(e\lambda)$ has mass $e^{-e\lambda}(e\lambda)^y/y!$ for $y\in\mathbb N_0$, with $e\ge0,\lambda>0$ (when $e=0$ it is concentrated at zero); Dirichlet$(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k)$ has density $\Gamma(\sum_j\alpha_j)\prod_jp_j^{\alpha_j-1}/\prod_j\Gamma(\alpha_j)$ relative to Lebesgue measure $dp_1\cdots dp_{k-1}$ on $p_j>0,\sum_{j<k}p_j<1$, with $p_k=1-\sum_{j<k}p_j$; and Multinomial$(n,p)$ has mass $n!\prod_jp_j^{y_j}/\prod_jy_j!$ on integer counts $y_j\ge0,\sum_jy_j=n$. Require $\alpha,\beta>0$, Gamma shape/rate positive, and every Dirichlet coordinate positive. Then give exact Beta–Binomial update $\mathrm{Beta}(\alpha+y,\beta+n-y)$ for integer $0\le y\le n$; exposure-adjusted Gamma–Poisson update $\mathrm{Gamma}(a+\sum_i y_i,b+\sum_i e_i)$ for independent counts and proper prior; Normal–Normal update for independent $Y_i\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2)$, known $\sigma^2>0$, prior $\mu\sim N(\mu_0,\tau_0^2)$ with $\tau_0^2>0$, variance $V_n=(\tau_0^{-2}+n\sigma^{-2})^{-1}$ and mean $V_n(\mu_0/\tau_0^2+n\bar y/\sigma^2)$; and Dirichlet–multinomial update $\alpha_j+y_j$. Prove Dirichlet normalization by iterated Beta integrals; do not claim the converse characterization of regular exponential families. Define the reusable Gaussian conditioner: for $X\in\mathbb R^d,Y\in\mathbb R^m$ jointly Gaussian with mean $(a,b)$ and PSD block covariance $\begin{pmatrix}A&C\\C^T&B\end{pmatrix}$, if $B\succ0$ the everywhere-defined Gaussian version of $\mathcal L(X\mid Y=y)$ has mean $a+CB^{-1}(y-b)$ and PSD covariance $A-CB^{-1}C^T$; $A$ and the conditional covariance may be singular. Exclude singular-$B$ pseudoinverse formulas.

design_contract.scope: When the posterior is supplied as a measurable kernel $y\mapsto\Pi_y$ by the standard-Borel disintegration route in BCS-01 or the dominated formula in BCS-02, define posterior predictive $Q_y^{pred}(A)=\int Q_\theta(A)\Pi_y(d\theta)$ for future probability kernel $Q_\theta$. Under finite second moments prove $E(\tilde Y|y)=E_{\Pi_y}E(\tilde Y|\theta)$ and $\operatorname{Var}(\tilde Y|y)=E_{\Pi_y}\operatorname{Var}(\tilde Y|\theta)+\operatorname{Var}_{\Pi_y}E(\tilde Y|\theta)$. Define a credible set as a measurable set $C(y)$ with $\Pi_y(C(y))\ge1-\alpha$; central quantile intervals are one choice, while HPD sets require a density and may be disconnected/nonunique. Given a measurable action space and loss $L(\theta,a)$, define posterior risk only when the integral is finite; call $a^*(y)$ a Bayes action only when it is a measurable minimizer and the minimum is attained. Under $E_{\Pi_y}\theta^2<\infty$, squared loss uniquely gives the posterior mean; under $E_{\Pi_y}|\theta|<\infty$, absolute loss is minimized by any posterior median; finite-class zero–one loss is minimized by a class of maximal posterior mass. The squared-loss proof inherits the Axiom-of-Choice assumption from the published L2-projection supplier. Do not assert pointwise zero–one MAP optimality for a continuous parameter. Posterior credibility is not a frequentist coverage theorem.
design_contract.proof_route: Tonelli/conditional integration for prediction; expand conditional second moments; squared-loss posterior mean follows from the checked L2 projection theorem; median and finite-class actions follow by direct loss comparison; use MSF-03 only under its measurable attained-minimizer contract.

design_contract.scope: On standard-Borel group and parameter spaces, define a jointly measurable hyperparameter kernel $\eta\mapsto G_\eta$ and conditional observation kernels. Given a proper hyperprior $\Pi_\eta$ and conditional independence, form $\Pi_\eta(d\eta)\prod_jG_\eta(d\theta_j)f_j(y_j\mid\theta_j)$; call its normalization a joint posterior only on an observation fibre with positive finite evidence. For known-variance normal random effects with $s_j^2>0$ and $\tau^2>0$, derive $\theta_j\mid\mu,\tau,y_j\sim N(\hat\theta_j,V_j)$ where $\hat\theta_j=(\bar y_j/s_j^2+\mu/\tau^2)/(1/s_j^2+1/\tau^2)$ and $V_j=(1/s_j^2+1/\tau^2)^{-1}$. This is conditional shrinkage; when hyperparameters are unknown, integrate their joint posterior rather than plug them in silently. Define current-group prediction by integrating over that group’s posterior and new-group prediction by first drawing $\theta_{new}\sim G_\eta$ and integrating over the posterior of $(\eta,\theta_{new})$. Finite exchangeability is a modeling assumption and does not imply a mixture-of-iid representation; no de Finetti theorem is claimed here.

design_contract.scope: For each model with proper parameter prior define evidence $m_i(y)=\int f_i(y\mid\theta_i)\Pi_i(d\theta_i)$ using a jointly measurable likelihood kernel and a common data dominating measure. For finite model space and positive prior model weights $w_i$ summing to one, when every evidence is finite positive prove $P(M_i\mid y)=w_im_i(y)/\sum_jw_jm_j(y)$ and posterior odds equal prior odds times $BF_{21}=m_2/m_1$. A point null needs positive prior mass/explicit model atom; a purely continuous prior assigns it zero. Arbitrarily scaled improper priors do not define generic evidence or Bayes factors. Define Type-II maximum marginal likelihood $\hat\eta(y)\in\arg\max_\eta m(y\mid\eta)$ only when that maximizer exists, and define the plug-in posterior $\Pi(d\theta\mid y,\hat\eta(y))$; contrast with full Bayes retaining hyperparameter uncertainty/cross-group dependence. State no generic EB risk, consistency, dominance or credible-coverage guarantee. For the balanced one-way normal random-effects model $Y_{ij}=\mu+a_i+\epsilon_{ij}$, $i=1,\ldots,k$, $j=1,\ldots,r$, with $k,r\ge2$, independent $a_i\sim N(0,\tau^2)$ and $\epsilon_{ij}\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$, define $MSB=\frac{r}{k-1}\sum_i(\bar Y_{i\cdot}-\bar Y_{\cdot\cdot})^2$ and $MSW=\frac1{k(r-1)}\sum_{i,j}(Y_{ij}-\bar Y_{i\cdot})^2$. Then $E(MSB)=\sigma^2+r\tau^2$, $E(MSW)=\sigma^2$, so the method-of-moments estimate is $(MSB-MSW)/r$; it may be negative, and truncating at zero changes the method and does not prove a structural zero.

design_contract.scope: Let $B$ be a real separable Banach space and $W$ a centered tight Borel Gaussian random element with law $\mu$. Use `def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces` and `def-strongly-measurable-banach-valued-function`: since $B$ is separable and $W$ is Borel measurable, countable dense centers and measurable nearest-center cells give finite-valued simple approximants converging pointwise to $W$, so $W$ is strongly measurable. First name and prove the Fernique prerequisite: for some $a>0$, $E\exp(a\|W\|_B^2)<\infty$, hence $E\|W\|_B^2<\infty$. For each $\ell\in B^*$, $x\mapsto\ell(x)x$ preserves strong measurability and $\ell(W)$ is a scalar Gaussian with finite second moment; Cauchy–Schwarz gives $E[|\ell(W)|\|W\|_B]<\infty$. Reuse the Bochner integrability criterion to define $C:B^*\to B$ by the Bochner expectation $C\ell=E[\ell(W)W]$; the Bochner norm inequality bounds $\|C\ell\|_B$, and bounded linear maps commute with this integral. The covariance RKHS $\mathbb H$ is the completion of $C(B^*)$ under $\langle C\ell,C\ell'\rangle_{\mathbb H}=E[\ell(W)\ell'(W)]$, quotienting zero-norm functionals; the inner-product formula follows by applying the bounded functional $\ell$ to $C\ell'$ inside the Bochner integral. Name and prove the Cameron–Martin translation identity: for $h=C\ell\in\mathbb H$, $\mu_h(A):=\Pr(W+h\in A)=\int_A\exp\{\ell(x)-\frac12E[\ell(W)^2]\}\,\mu(dx)$ for Borel $A$; establish independence of the representative and equality of measures from Gaussian characteristic functions on a countable norming family. Then prove $\operatorname{supp}(\mu)=\overline{\mathbb H}^{\,B}$: use Hahn–Banach separation and $E[\ell(W)^2]=0$ for the inclusion into the closure, and prove $0\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu)$ from tightness/separability and the Gaussian difference law before applying translation equivalence for the reverse inclusion. State the separable-Banach Borell bound $\Pr(\|W\|_B>E\|W\|_B+r)\le e^{-r^2/(2\sigma_W^2)}$ for $r\ge0$ when $\sigma_W^2=\sup_{\ell\in B^*,\|\ell\|_{B^*}\le1}E[\ell(W)^2]>0$; if $\sigma_W=0$, then $W=0$ almost surely and the tail probability is zero. Define $\phi_{w_0}(\epsilon)=\inf_{\|h-w_0\|_B<\epsilon}\|h\|_{\mathbb H}^2-\log\Pr(\|W\|_B<\epsilon)$. Under $w_0\in\overline{\mathbb H}^{\,B}$, $\epsilon_n>0$, $e^{-Cn\epsilon_n^2}<1/2$ for $C>1$, and $\phi_{w_0}(\epsilon_n)\le n\epsilon_n^2$, state the source sieve: a measurable $B_n$ has $\log N(3\epsilon_n,B_n,\|\cdot\|_B)\le6Cn\epsilon_n^2$, $\Pr(W\notin B_n)\le e^{-Cn\epsilon_n^2}$, and $\Pr(\|W-w_0\|_B<2\epsilon_n)\ge e^{-n\epsilon_n^2}$. The posterior theorem additionally needs the statistical distance/KL quantities controlled by this Banach norm.

design_contract.scope: On a standard-Borel space $(\mathsf X,\mathcal A)$ with finite nonzero base measure $\alpha$, a Dirichlet process $G\sim DP(\alpha)$ is a measurable random element of $\mathcal P(\mathsf X)$ equipped with the evaluation sigma-algebra, whose masses on every finite measurable partition $(A_1,\ldots,A_k)$ have the Dirichlet law with parameters $(\alpha(A_j))$ after omitting zero-parameter cells (zero-base cells have mass zero almost surely). Finite-partition laws alone specify only cylinder distributions, so prove existence of a countably additive measurable random probability measure. Use the following explicit normalized-gamma construction, rather than assuming a gamma process: on $\mathsf X\times(0,\infty)$ construct a Poisson random measure with sigma-finite intensity $\alpha(dx)t^{-1}e^{-t}dt$ by partitioning the mark axis into countably many finite-intensity strips, drawing independent Poisson counts and conditionally IID atoms on each strip, and proving independent-count laws by Poisson thinning. Set $\Gamma(A)=\sum_{(x,t):x\in A}t$; prove measurable evaluations, $E\Gamma(\mathsf X)=\alpha(\mathsf X)<\infty$, and $E e^{-s\Gamma(A)}=(1+s)^{-\alpha(A)}$. Thus disjoint increments are independent Gamma$(\alpha(A),1)$ variables and the total is finite and strictly positive almost surely; on the exceptional null event assign a fixed probability measure. Then $G(A)=\Gamma(A)/\Gamma(\mathsf X)$ is a measurable countably additive random probability with the Dirichlet partition laws. Under conditionally IID observations $X_i|G\sim G$, prove kernel measurability of $x_{1:n}\mapsto DP(\alpha+\sum_i\delta_{x_i})$ on finite partition cylinders; verify its disintegration identity against data rectangles by Dirichlet–multinomial conjugacy on a common refinement, then extend by a monotone-class argument to the evaluation sigma-algebra and $\mathcal A^{\otimes n}$. It is a posterior version with predictive $P(X_{n+1}\in A|X_{1:n})=(\alpha(A)+\sum_i1_{X_i\in A})/(\alpha(\mathsf X)+n)$. A measurable $\alpha$-null data event has prior-predictive probability zero and only a version choice there; individual points having zero point-mass probability under a diffuse law does not itself make their posterior update exceptional. Do not assert a general weak-support theorem without a topology and complete prior-mass proof; process definition/update alone does not imply density consistency or contraction.

design_contract.scope: In white noise $dX^{(n)}=f_0dt+n^{-1/2}dW$, define the Hilbert space $H(\delta)=H^{-1/2,\delta}_2$ by $\|g\|_{H(\delta)}^2=\sum_l a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}\sum_k|\langle\psi_{lk},g\rangle|^2$, with $a_l=2^l$ for wavelets and $a_l=\max(2,|l|)$ for trigonometric coefficients. State the weak BvM precisely: with posterior $\Pi_n=\Pi(\cdot|X^{(n)})$, efficient center $X^{(n)}$ and canonical white-noise law $N$ on $H(\delta)$, $\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\Pi_n\circ[f\mapsto\sqrt n(f-X^{(n)})]^{-1},N)\to0$ in $P_{f_0}^n$-probability. The series condition $\sum_{l,k}\sigma_l^2<\infty$ follows from $\sum_l2^l2^{-2l(\alpha+1/2)}<\infty$, so the prior defines an $L^2$ random element almost surely. Require $f_0\in L^2$ and $\sup_{l,k}|\langle f_0,\psi_{lk}\rangle|/\sigma_l\le M$; Theorem 9 also requires continuity of $\varphi$ at each normalized true coefficient. The source's $C^\beta$ truth and $\alpha\le\beta$ condition is one sufficient route to the coefficient bound, not an extra premise of Theorem 9. title: Finite-horizon SMC error, CLTs, and degeneracy
breadth_depth_assessment: Fixed-horizon particle CLT now contains recursive moment class and multinomial/residual variance equations; restrictive long-time variance theorem is not finite-N uniform accuracy.
findings_and_repairs: Fixed-horizon particle CLT now contains recursive moment class and multinomial/residual variance equations; restrictive long-time variance theorem is not finite-N uniform accuracy.

design_contract.scope: State Chopin's fixed-horizon $H\to\infty$ particle-count CLT with targets $\pi_t$, proposal laws $\tilde\pi_t$, incremental weights $\upsilon_t=d\pi_t/d\tilde\pi_t$, and mutation kernels $k_t$. For vector-valued $\phi$, initialize $\Phi_0^{(d)}=\{\phi:E_{\tilde\pi_0}\|\phi\|^2<\infty\}$ and recursively require $\phi\in\Phi_t^{(d)}$ if for some $\delta>0$, $E_{\tilde\pi_t}\|\upsilon_t\phi\|^{2+\delta}<\infty$ and $\theta_{t-1}\mapsto E_{k_t(\theta_{t-1},\cdot)}[\upsilon_t\phi]$ belongs to $\Phi_{t-1}^{(d)}$. Require $1\in\Phi_t^{(1)}$ at every time. Give the exact variance recursion $\widetilde V_0(\phi)=\operatorname{Var}_{\tilde\pi_0}(\phi)$, $\widetilde V_t(\phi)=\widehat V_{t-1}(E_{k_t}\phi)+E_{\pi_{t-1}}[\operatorname{Var}_{k_t}(\phi)]$, $V_t(\phi)=\widetilde V_t(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi))$, and, for multinomial resampling, $\widehat V_t(\phi)=V_t(\phi)+\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\phi)$. For residual resampling replace the last term by $R_t(\phi)=E_{\tilde\pi_t}[r(\upsilon_t)\phi\phi^T]-E_{\tilde\pi_t}[r(\upsilon_t)\phi]E_{\tilde\pi_t}[r(\upsilon_t)\phi]^T/E_{\tilde\pi_t}[r(\upsilon_t)]$, where $r(u)=u-\lfloor u\rfloor$, so $\widehat V_t=V_t+R_t$ when $E_{\tilde\pi_t}r(\upsilon_t)>0$; if this expectation is zero, all residual offspring counts are deterministic and define $R_t=0$. State both source CLT outputs (weighted estimate variance $V_t$ and post-resampling unweighted estimate variance $\widehat V_t$), centered at $\pi_t\phi$. For a separate bounded-asymptotic-variance-in-time result, require finite test oscillation $\Delta\phi$, uniform transition and proposal density ratios $g(x|x')/g(x|x'')\le C$, $q_t(x|x')/q_t(x|x'')\le C$, and likelihoods $0<f\le f(y|x)\le\bar f$; this is Chopin Theorem 5's restrictive asymptotic-variance condition, not a general finite-$N$ time-uniform error bound. ESS is weight concentration, not posterior coverage/variance/convergence; a fixed-horizon CLT is not a uniform-in-time accuracy guarantee.

design_contract.scope: Let a finite group $G$ act measurably on the sample space and assume the null law is invariant: $X\overset d=gX$ for every $g\in G$. For the full orbit, the nonrandomized upper-tail rank p-value $|G|^{-1}\#\{g:T(gX)\ge T(X)\}$ is super-uniform; randomizing uniformly within the tied boundary rank yields an exactly uniform null p-value. For Monte Carlo, draw $B$ transformations IID uniformly from $G$ independently of $X$ and include identity as the distinguished $(B+1)$-st transformation; use $p_+=(1+\sum_{b=1}^B1\{T(g_bX)\ge T(X)\})/(B+1)$, which is super-uniform under ties. If sampling a subset without replacement, state its uniform-subset design and the source's rank argument separately; do not transfer the with-replacement formula without proof. The uncorrected $B^{-1}\sum 1\{T(g_bX)\ge T(X)\}$ can be anti-conservative and can equal zero. Keep sharp-null assignment inference (SME-12) distinct from IID distribution-invariance permutation inference.
design_contract.proof_route: Condition on the orbit and use the group action to make the observed rank uniform up to ties; for Monte Carlo, condition on the identity-containing random transformation list and apply the exchangeable-rank argument.

design_contract.scope: Under $P=Q$, exchangeability gives finite-sample exactness (BCS-51). For the two-sample order-$(r,r)$ U-statistic route, take independent IID $X_1,\ldots,X_m\sim P$ and $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\sim Q$, fixed $r\le\min(m,n)$, $m/(m+n)\to p\in(0,1)$, and a measurable kernel $h$ symmetric within each block and antisymmetric when the $X$ and $Y$ blocks are exchanged. Define $U_{m,n}$ as the average of $h$ over all $\binom mr\binom nr$ index pairs and $\theta(P,Q)=E_{P^r\otimes Q^r}h$. Under weak null $\theta(P,Q)=0$, require $0<E[h^2]<\infty$ for every assignment of $P$- and $Q$-distributed arguments to the kernel positions, as in Chung–Romano Theorem 3.1. For $\bar P=pP+(1-p)Q$, define $h_{P,Q}^X(x)=\int h(x,x_2,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_r)P^{r-1}(dx_{2:r})Q^r(dy_{1:r})-\theta$ and $h_{P,Q}^Y(y)=\int h(x_1,\ldots,x_r,y,y_2,\ldots,y_r)P^r(dx_{1:r})Q^{r-1}(dy_{2:r})-\theta$, with the corresponding pooled projection $h_{\bar P}(z)=\int h(z,z_2,\ldots,z_r,z_{r+1},\ldots,z_{2r})\bar P^{2r-1}(dz_{2:2r})$; antisymmetry and equal pooled blocks give $E_{\bar P}h_{\bar P}=0$. Require positive finite $L^2(P)$, $L^2(Q)$ and $L^2(\bar P)$ norms for the respective first projections. Prove the Hoeffding decomposition, show its degenerate remainder is $o_P((m+n)^{-1/2})$ under the fixed-order second-moment premises, and derive the sampling CLT from the projected IID sums. For permutation studentization use consistent estimators $\hat\sigma_m^2\to E_P[(h_{P,Q}^X)^2]$, $\hat\sigma_n^2\to E_Q[(h_{P,Q}^Y)^2]$, and, under IID $\bar P$ samples, $\hat\sigma_m^2,\hat\sigma_n^2\to E_{\bar P}[h_{\bar P}^2]$; define $V_{m,n}=r\{\hat\sigma_m^2/m+\hat\sigma_n^2/n\}^{1/2}$ and $S_{m,n}=U_{m,n}/V_{m,n}$. The Chung–Romano theorem then gives the permutation cdf of $\sqrt m S_{m,n}$ converging uniformly in probability to $\Phi$, and the same studentized true-sampling limit follows from its projection CLT and consistent variance estimates. Mere positive kernel second moment does not exclude a degenerate first projection. Unstudentized Wilcoxon is not licensed under a weak mean/median null by the exact $P=Q$ result.

design_contract.scope: Define geometrically refined levels $h_l=M^{-l}T$, coupled corrections and telescoping expectation. Require independent level estimators and rates: bias $O(h_L^\alpha)$, $\alpha\ge1/2$; correction variance $O(N_l^{-1}h_l^\beta)$, $\beta>0$; cost $O(N_lh_l^{-1})$. State complexity for MSE $\epsilon^2$: $O(\epsilon^{-2})$ if $\beta>1$, $O(\epsilon^{-2}\log^2(\epsilon^{-1}))$ if $\beta=1$, and $O(\epsilon^{-2-(1-\beta)/\alpha})$ if $\beta<1$. The requested square-integrable Euler–Maruyama case uses independent pre-category designs P-NUM-SDE-01/02. Under P-NUM-SDE-01's globally Lipschitz and linear-growth state bounds, $1/2$-Hölder time modulus, adapted initial condition independent of future Brownian increments, and $X_0\in L^2$, a separate local interpolation-error/Itô-isometry/BDG/Grönwall proof gives $E\sup_{t\le T}|X(t)-X^h(t)|^2=O(h)$. With shared Brownian increments on adjacent levels, the $L^2$ triangle inequality gives $E|X_{h_l}(T)-X_{h_{l-1}}(T)|^2=O(h_l)$; for a globally Lipschitz payoff this gives correction variance $O(h_l)$ and path cost $O(h_l^{-1})$, so $\beta=1$. The strong bound alone gives Lipschitz-payoff bias $O(h_L^{1/2})$, hence $\alpha=1/2$ and complexity $O(\epsilon^{-2}\log^2(\epsilon^{-1}))$. This direct finite-$L^2$ proof is a separate local route and is not inferred from Higham–Mao–Stuart. Their source theorem supports the same rate under its exact autonomous contract: $C^1$ drift/diffusion, one-sided Lipschitz drift, globally Lipschitz diffusion, polynomial local-Lipschitz drift, and uniform moments of every order for the exact solution, step process, and continuous interpolation; the globally Lipschitz/linear-growth specialization obtains these moments from an all-moment initial condition. For weak order one, require the separate P-NUM-SDE-02 bounded-test/backward-Kolmogorov contract: $u(t,x)=E[\varphi(X_T^{t,x})]$ solves the backward equation, lies in $C^{2,4}$ with time derivatives through order two and space derivatives through order four bounded by $C(1+\|x\|^q)$, and exact/Euler processes have uniform moments of order $p\ge2q+8$. The local one-step expected Taylor remainder is $O(h^2)(1+\|x\|^{q+4})$; telescoping gives bias $O(h_L)$, so $\alpha=1$. When this payoff is also Lipschitz, $\beta=1$ remains and the same logarithmic complexity follows. Lipschitz payoff alone does not give weak order one.

design_contract.scope: Define an RQMC set $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ on $[0,1]^d$ by marginal uniformity $X_i\sim U([0,1]^d)$ (the points need not be independent) and a separate low-discrepancy property. For integrable $f$, the single-rule estimator $\hat I=n^{-1}\sum_i f(X_i)$ is unbiased. For $R\ge2$ independent full-set randomizations with estimates $\hat I_1,\ldots,\hat I_R$, the replicate variance estimator is $[R(R-1)]^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^R(\hat I_r-\bar I_R)^2$; it estimates randomization variance, and a Student interval requires additional replicate-distribution assumptions. Keep point count $n$ separate from randomization count $R$. For a nested uniform scramble of a $(0,m,d)$-net in base $b\ge\max(d,2)$, and $f\in L^2([0,1]^d)$ with variance $\sigma^2$, state Owen's exact bound $\operatorname{Var}(\hat I)\le (b/(b-1))^{\min(m,d-1)}\sigma^2/n\le e\sigma^2/n$. For a nested uniform scramble of a $(\lambda,t,m,d)$-net with $n=\lambda b^m$, $1\le\lambda<b$, also state the source's faster bound $\operatorname{Var}(\hat I)=O(n^{-3}(\log n)^{d-1})$ only when all mixed partial derivatives using each of the $d$ distinct coordinates once are continuous on $[0,1]^d$. Do not promise a general CLT; small $R$ may give poor interval coverage.
